romundina:enwiki:3.title: Romundina (Dentition and the evolution of teeth)

facts.statement: The first Romundina specimen was discovered in 1975 by Swedish paleontologist Tor Ørvig on Prince of Wales Island in Nunavut.
facts.quote: The first specimen of Romundina was originally discovered by Swedish paleontologist Tor Ørvig in 1975 on Prince of Wales Island (Nunavut)

facts.statement: Only one species, Romundina stellina, has been described for this genus.
facts.quote: Only one known species of Romundina has been discovered which was named Romundina stellina by Ørvig

facts.statement: Romundina lived between 400 and 419 million years ago during the Early Devonian.
facts.quote: Romundina are believed to have lived on Earth between 400 and 419 million years ago

facts.statement: Romundina was a small, heavily armored acanthothoracid placoderm that lived in shallow marine environments.
facts.quote: Romundina is a small, heavily armored extinct genus of acanthothoracid placoderms which lived in shallow marine environments

facts.statement: The species name stellina refers to the star-shaped tubercles that ornamented its dermal skeleton.
facts.quote: The species name stellina refers to stellate (derived from Latin word stella meaning star) tubercles that the Placoderm has ornamenting its dermal skeleton

facts.statement: Romundina likely possessed a vascular spine growing just behind the head that served a defensive role.
facts.quote: Additionally, Romundina likely had a vascular spine which grew posteriorly and proximally from the cranial side of the spine just posterior of the head

facts.statement: Research suggests Romundina primarily ate invertebrates such as crustaceans and worms.
facts.quote: Research suggests that Romundina also ate mostly invertebrates such as crustaceans and worms

facts.statement: Romundina's large crushing tooth-like structures and gnathal plates were likely adapted for eating organisms with hard shells like crustaceans.
facts.quote: Romundina's large crushing tooth-like structures as well as the large gnathal plates would appear to be useful in eating organisms with hard shells such as crustaceans

facts.statement: There is debate over whether the tooth-like structures and gnathal plates of Romundina represent the true primitive condition of Gnathostome dentition.
facts.quote: There is currently much debate surrounding whether these tooth-like structures as well as the gnathal plates they sit on can be seen as the true primitive condition of Gnathostome dentition

facts.statement: The primitive tooth-like structures on Romundina's supragnathal plates have a multi-cuspid appearance suggesting tooth-to-tooth occlusion occurred.
facts.quote: These primitive tooth-like structures lie on supragnathal plates and have a multi-cuspid appearance suggesting some degree of tooth-to-tooth occlusion occurred

facts.statement: Romundina's disorganized dental tubercles resemble the primitive features of Cyclostomes, suggesting organized tooth rows evolved just before the first Gnathostomes.
facts.quote: Romundina's dental tubercles lack any apparent organization which is a more primitive feature found in Cyclostomes suggesting that organized tooth rows evolved just prior to the evolution of the first Gnathostomes

facts.statement: The Romundina skull consisted of thin dermal bones heavily ornamented with star-shaped tubercles rich in mesodentine.
facts.quote: The skull of Romundina consists of thin proportional dermal bones, which are heavily ornamented by mesodentine rich stellate (star shaped) tubercles

facts.statement: The star-shaped tubercles on Romundina's skull were likely used for protection against predators.
facts.quote: These stellate tubercles were likely used as a form of protection from predators

facts.statement: Romundina is distinguished from previous placoderms by the absence of tesserae between dermal bones on the skull roof, which were fused together.
facts.quote: An additional feature that distinguishes Romundina from previous Placoderms is the absence of tesserae (a type of mineralized tile) between the dermal bones on the roof of the skull as the dermal bones in the roof of Romundina's skull are fused together

facts.statement: Romundina unambiguously possessed a jaw, but its cranial anatomy and brain proportions were more closely aligned with jawless vertebrates.
facts.quote: Romundina has been shown to unambiguously have a jaw, however the cranial anatomy and proportions of the brain are more closely aligned with those of jawless vertebrates

facts.statement: Romundina had a large protruding bony upper lip that began anterior to the nasal capsule.
facts.quote: Furthermore, Romundina have a large protruding bony upper "lip", which begins anteriorly to the nasal capsule

facts.statement: Fossils of corals and other shallow-water organisms found with Romundina suggest it lived in relatively shallow water.
facts.quote: Corals and other shallow water organisms were also found alongside Romundina in the same formation on Prince of Wales Island suggesting that they too lived in relatively shallow water

facts.statement: The genus Romundina was discovered in 1975 by the Norwegian paleontologist Tor Ørvig.
facts.quote: Romundina was discovered by a Norwegian paleontologist named Tor Ørvig in 1975.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in rocks collected by the geologist Dr. Rómundur Thorsteinsson and later provided to Ørvig for study.
facts.quote: The fossil was discovered in rocks collected by geologist Dr. Rómundur Thorsteinsson that were later given to Ørvig to search for fossils.

facts.statement: The specimen was found in a 0.5-meter layer taken from the middle of a 12-meter section of unnamed carbonate rocks at locality C-8234.
facts.quote: The rock sample, which was given to Tor Ørvig to study (and that Romundina was discovered in), was a 0.5 m layer which taken from the middle of a 12 m section of unnamed carbonate rocks from the locality C-8234.

facts.statement: Tor Ørvig prepared the fossil using a mixture of formic and acetic acid to remove the surrounding rock and reveal a three-dimensional specimen.
facts.quote: Ørvig prepared the specimen by using a combination of formic and acetic acid to eat away the rocks, leaving a fully preserved three-dimensional Romundina specimen.

facts.statement: The original specimen consisted mainly of a head with a complete dermal skull roof and endocranial elements, lacking most of the body.
facts.quote: The specimen initially discovered consisted of a head with mostly complete dermal skull-roof and associated endocranial elements, which lacked most of the body segments.

facts.statement: The most commonly cited specimen is MNHN.F.CPW1, a three-dimensionally preserved fossil discovered by Ørvig in 1975.
facts.quote: Currently, the most commonly cited Romundina specimen is specimen MNHN.F.CPW1, which was originally discovered by Ørvig in 1975 and is preserved three-dimensionally.

facts.statement: Known specimens of Romundina are housed at the National Museum of Natural History in Paris, France.
facts.quote: MNHN.F.CPW1, as well as the other known specimens, are kept at the National Museum of Natural History in Paris, France.

facts.statement: Romundina fossils were found near a stream in carbonate rock formations on the western side of Prince of Wales Island in the Canadian Arctic.
facts.quote: The Romundina specimens were found near a stream in an unnamed formation of carbonate rocks on the western side Prince of Wales Island in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago.

facts.statement: The environment where Romundina lived was likely a shallow water or tidal reef.
facts.quote: This suggests that the geological environment was most likely a shallow water or tidal reef.

facts.statement: The first Romundina specimen was found in rock dating to the Lochkovian age of the Silurian period.
facts.quote: The region where the first Romundina specimen was found lying beside the westernmost stretches of the Peel Sound Formation in rock, which dates to the Lochkovian age of the Silurian period.

facts.statement: During the Silurian period, Prince of Wales Island was located close to the equator.
facts.quote: The land that makes up Prince of Wales Island would have been located close to the equator during the Silurian period.

facts.statement: Romundina likely lived in relatively warm waters with an average temperature of around 30 °C (86 °F).
facts.quote: Additionally, the average water temperature would have been around 30 °C (86 °F) suggesting that Romundina tended to live in relatively warm waters when compared with the average water temperature today.

facts.statement: Romundina is characterized as being in the middle of the Placoderm grade.
facts.quote: Romundina is commonly characterized as being in the middle of the Placoderm grade.

facts.statement: The species name of the animal is Romundina stellina.
facts.quote: name: Romundina stellina

facts.statement: Romundina belongs to the kingdom Animalia.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia

facts.statement: Romundina is classified within the phylum Chordata.
facts.quote: phylum: Chordata

facts.statement: Romundina is classified in the class Placodermi.
facts.quote: classis: Placodermi

facts.statement: Romundina belongs to the order Acanthothoraci.
facts.quote: ordo: Acanthothoraci

facts.statement: Romundina is part of the family Palaeacanthaspidae.
facts.quote: familia: Palaeacanthaspidae

facts.statement: The species was described by Ørvig in 1975.
facts.quote: species_authority: Ørvig, 1975

facts.statement: Romundina stellina was an extinct placoderm of the family Palaeacanthaspidae that lived during the Early Devonian in Canada.
facts.quote: Romundina stellina es una especie extinta de placodermo de la familia Palaeacanthaspidae que vivió durante el Devónico Inferior en Canadá.

facts.statement: Romundina lived between 419.62 and 393.47 million years ago, spanning from the Lochkovian to the Emsian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Emsian (419.62 to 393.47 million years ago)

facts.statement: A phylogenetic and morphological analysis by Dupret et al. (2014) suggests Romundina is related to basal members of the Arthrodira clade.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético y morfológico realizado por Dupret et al. (2014) sugiere que está relacionado con miembros basales del clado Arthrodira.

facts.statement: The same formation as Romundina contains fossils of arthrodires, heterostracans, gastropods, cephalopods, and corals.
facts.quote: Other species found in this formation include arthrodires, the heterostracans Althaspis, Dinaspidella, and Traquairaspis, gastropods, cephalopods, as well as fossil evidence of both colonial and solitary Corals.
